results.title: Introducing Video Editor in Manus 2.0: Anyone Can Now Make A Video Worth Posting
results.content:
Manus can make everything a video needs on the spot: shots from video models like Seedance 2.5, plus images, music, voiceover and sound effects. But what's special is the code. Manus has its own computer, enabling it to write code for motion graphics, layouts, charts and map routes, render them, screenshot the result to check it, and keep fixing what it doesn't like. I've watched it draw a grid over a frame in Python to locate pixels, and use FFmpeg to turn 24 fps footage into 120 fps so a 5x slow-motion shot stays smooth. I never taught it that. It worked these tricks out to make the video better. Generated shots and code-made visuals can share one video. For BEAT RUSH, Manus generated a dancing anime character with Seedance, then built the rhythm-game interface and beat effects in code. [...] ﻿

 

﻿

 Edit it yourself, or just ask Manus. Frames from the launch film above You don't need editing experience to use Video Editor. You only need to know the feel you want.

### For creators: start from your own footage

Because Video Editor runs on your desktop, it can start from the footage already on your computer. Drag videos into the chat, or tell Manus which folder they're in, and it imports them and lays them on the timeline. 

﻿ [...] ### Every layer is its own track

Every ingredient Manus uses, from generated shots and images to captions, motion graphics, voiceover, music and sound effects, sits on its own layer of the Video Editor timeline. You don't get a flattened MP4. You get a video you can take apart and change. 

﻿

 A vlog clip split into eight layers, 30 seconds

### For everyone: drag it yourself, or just ask Manus

You can drag, trim, rewrite captions and set volume with your mouse, like in any editor. Or tell Manus "turn the music down" or "tighten this part." Both change the same project. When you hand it back, Manus picks up from your edits instead of starting over. 

﻿

results.title: Manus 2.0 AI Agents Expand the Product, but Trust Is the Real Test
results.content:
Regenerating the entire video could introduce new unwanted changes. Studio instead exposes clips, images, text, audio, and motion graphics as separate components on an editable timeline.

The user can make a direct change, then return the project to the agent for another pass. That creates a mixed workflow where manual editing and automated generation can alternate.

Manus says its Video Editor targets product advertisements, tutorials, vlogs, motion graphics, and AI-generated user-style content. The company specifies a focus on videos lasting 30 to 60 seconds.

The release also adds Alchemy mode, which combines video generation and code generation under an automated creative-direction process. Manus claims this mode improves composition, detail, motion, and pacing. [...] ## Manus Studio Blends Generation With Direct Editing

Manus is betting that agents become more useful when users can inspect and edit their output without restarting the entire generation process.

The company has renamed and expanded its desktop experience as Manus Studio. It describes Studio as a shared workspace where people and AI can work on documents, spreadsheets, PDFs, presentations, websites, code, games, and video.

This design pushes against a recurring limitation of prompt-based creative tools. Generating an acceptable first draft can be fast, while correcting one specific element can become frustrating.

Manus illustrates the problem with video editing. A user might like an automatically generated advertisement but want to replace its music or use a different product image.

results.title: Manus releases 2.0 with new agent architecture, video editor, and game development tools - UpTech Media
results.content:
Clips, images, text, motion graphics and audio appear as separate pieces that users can swap, move or replace with their own footage. Manus can then take another pass that works from those edits.

Manus said the tool targets short product ads of 30 to 60 seconds, AI-generated user content, data motion graphics, tutorials, vlogs, and motion-led videos.

Video Editor also includes Alchemy mode, in which Manus handles creative direction using video and code generation together. The company claimed the mode brings better ideas, tighter control of visual detail, more polished motion and improved pacing, and said users can still fine-tune results on the timeline. [...] Users configure a workflow through a single prompt. “Just tell Manus in a single prompt what to watch and what to do next, and it sets up and runs the workflow,” the company said.

The desktop app has been renamed Manus Studio, which Manus describes as “a shared workspace for people and AI.” Studio loads only the tools a project requires, which the company says keeps Manus focused on the task at hand.

The release upgrades Studio for documents, spreadsheets, PDFs, slides, websites and code. It also adds two new professional environments, Video Editor and Game Dev.

Video Editor addresses a limitation of earlier versions, where changing a generated video meant writing a new prompt and regenerating the whole clip. Now, the company said, “Manus gives you the timeline instead.” [...] In Cue, each agent has its own email, phone number, wallet, and computer. Agents can send messages, pay within a user-set budget, take calls and leave a summary in the app.

Users can also place several agents in a group chat with a shared goal, so that they hand work to one another. “You set the direction and make the final call,” Manus said.

Cue also connects to everyday services. At a restaurant, for example, a user can scan a QR code and the agent can order or hold a place in line.

Manus closed the announcement by framing the release around its founding aim, which is to help people turn ideas into something real, and Manus 2.0 keeps that promise.
